correctness.rationale: The powered distances on KG(3k-2,k) are 1, 2 or 3, with intersection size one exactly distance three. The Johnson scheme gives exact eigenvalues Lambda_j; direct A_k A_1 counting determines the intersection-one eigenvalues. The analytic inequalities bound all j≠2 strictly below the critical root for every k>=8, proving negative type and the Hilbert-rank drop. The k=7 counterexample uses exact rational hundredth-power bounds. The asymptotics follow from the unique-root expansion. The independent-inclusion arithmetic program was executed successfully; finite experiments are not substituted for general proof.

originality.rationale: The three-point powered distance modes of the diameter-three Kneser family are not covered by the general finite negative-type matrix algorithms or the published Euclidean bilipschitz distortion results. The new claim proves the second Johnson mode uniquely dominates all other modes at the first root for every integer k>=8, with a sharp k=7 counterexample and a derived exponential asymptotic. Classical scheme eigenvalues are expressly prior facts. The closest published and research-record searches did not identify a stronger covering theorem; priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The first diameter-three Kneser sequence has an exact critical Hilbert snowflake power for all k>=8. The competing Johnson representation switches by the sharp boundary k=7 versus k=8, the limiting power decreases exponentially, and the endpoint embedding dimension loses an explicit large representation. This identifies a structurally motivated spectral phase boundary for a natural graph-metric family, beyond a generic small numerical table.
